title: Artists dropped when the next hot act comes and who owns the masters
summary: She says labels move on to the next hot artist and some masters may revert to the artist; she credits the union and Paul Howard.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Because it's been a sort of a sore spot and it's been a little bitter spot with many people like myself, you know, who -- you've made records and you know the records have made money, but when the records -- when they stop selling a big sum, a terrific amount of records, they're looking for the next one. Who's next? Who's the next hot one? Then somebody else is going to come along and push the next artist, build you up, build the next artist up, and then you fall by the wayside. It doesn't mean that you're a failure and that your records have not sold. It doesn't mean that at all, you see.

But somebody in the background is shrewd enough and smart enough to say, well, now, we have, you know, we've made money off her. Let's move on, now. Let's -- you know, let's move on. So the artist is left -- you're left sort of wondering if there's any fairness to this thing. Really, when you're looking at it from that angle. And even if it did happen, and as you say, the thing that a record company, I think, I feel,

like you just mentioned, that what the record companies, if they really have any soul and recognition for your creativeness, or creativity, I think it would be fair to say, well, now, we're going to issue a record. They have the masters. See, they still have the masters, and legally some of them don't even own the masters, but the artist is not aware of the fact that they can get the masters back. I've learned that too. I've learned that. I've learned that some of these masters that the record companies have, they don't even own them. They have them, but the artist doesn't know that he can go and get his records back.
You mean the master belongs to the artist?
After a period of time, in some instances, yes. In some instances.

Well, in some instances I have been told this. But, as I say, it depends on how they, you know, what the contract is, and of course this all goes back to a union thing. By the time -- you see, by the time all this happened, naturally I was into the union, you see, thanks to Paul Howard, got me involved in -- well, I had been in the union years, because I had been out here quite awhile when this all happened.
